children.name: Anadenus altivagus
children.description:
External: Pale gray-orange preserved, probably red-orange alive; usually unicolor but sometimes with black blotches (Wiktor 2001).

Internal: Club-shaped penis (broadened toward its base), with narrow epiphallus on its apex; hooked, hardened spines or bristles inside lower part of penis, and a single papilla inside its apex; massive spermatheca 2x penis length and with short, thick duct (Wiktor 2001).

Juveniles: Sometimes have lateral bands (Wiktor 2001).

Size: To 75 mm long preserved, mantle length to 43 mm, body width 24 mm; alive and extended, may be to 200 mm long, 40 mm wide (Wiktor 2001).

children.name: Anadenus blanfordi Godwin-Austen, 1882
children.description:
External: Preserved: dark yellow-brown, with some dark marks on the top of the dorsum; strongly diamond-shaped tubercles on skin (Wiktor 2001).

Internal: Short epiphallus; cylindrical penis, slightly narrowed in the middle, and with a small protuberance on one side of the apex; papilla inside the penis apex, and internal ridges along its length (Wiktor 2001)

Genitalia resemble those of A. yantzeensis (Wiktor et al. 2000).

children.name: Anadenus gonggashanensis Wiktor, D.-N.Chen & M.Wu, 2000
children.description:
External: Pale spot in the middle of the mantle (Wiktor et al. 2000).

Internal: Long vas deferens; long, coiled epiphallus that is encircled by penial retractor at punction with penis; penis narrow, widened at both ends, and rounded sac connected to anterior side of penis; papilla with tubercles inside the posterior end of the penis and long folds in the rest of the penis and attached sac; very large spermatheca, much longer than duct and equal to length of penis; spermatheca duct connects to oviduct; very short atrium; spermatheca 100 mm long with flagellum at one end (Wiktor et al. 2000).

Unique characters of A. gonggashanensis among Anadenus species are the rounded sac attached to penis and the narrowness of penis (Wiktor 2001).

children.name: Anadenus nepalensis Wiktor, 2001
children.description:
External: Light brown-cream, olive, or brown alive, sometimes with brown or black lateral streaks, chevron-patterns along the dorsum, or black spots; some have orange spot on mantle and two orange lateral stripes on tail; darker neck and mantle; pale orange-cream sole; thick-set body; low, fine wrinkles relative to its genus, with longitudinal lines separating blocks of tubercles (Wiktor 2001).

Internal: Internal shell 10 x 7 mm; club shaped penis broadened toward base; inside penis, a large, tongue-shaped, ridged ligula that has a digital process toward the penis's base; short epiphallus; spermatheca the length of the penis with short, relatively narrow duct (Wiktor 2001).

Genitalia similar to those of A. yangtzeensis and A. altivagus (Wiktor 2001).

Juveniles: More well-defined patterns and darker than adults (Wiktor 2001).

children.name: Anadenus parvipenis Wiktor, De-Niu & Ming, 2000
children.description:
External: Olive brown body and sole on preserved animals, with black lateral marks on mantle and sides below mantle, and tiny black spots over entire body and sole (Wiktor et al. 2000).

Internal: Penis conical and small, with tongue-shaped internal ligula; spermatheca 2x length of penis, long, and club-shaped, with spherical duct 1/2 its length; epiphallus 12x length of penis and thick; thick oviduct (Wiktor et al. 2000).

Unique characters of A. parvipenis among Anadenus species are small penis, very long and thick epiphallus, thin penial retractor muscle (Wiktor 2001).

children.name: Anadenus yangtzeensis Wiktor, De-Niu & Ming, 2000
children.description:
External: Preserved: reddish brown body and sole, sometimes with 0.5 mm diam black spots throughout and/or black marks on mantle and lateral stripe of black spots (Wiktor et al. 2000).

Internal: Penis expanding towards base, with small bent appendix on its apex, and large wrinkled ligula inside its base; short appendix on penis apex; spermatheca narrow and about as long as penis; epiphallus and vas deferens thin; genitalia similar to those of A. blanfordi (Wiktor et al. 2000).

Unique characters of A. yangtzeensis among Anadenus species are little black spots on body, relatively thin vas deferens and epiphallus, appendix on penis, large ligula in penis (Wiktor 2001).

children.name: Anadenus yunnanensis Wiktor, De-Niu & Ming, 2000
children.description:
External: Preserved: black body; strong, big wrinkles on dorsum with a triangular cross-section (Wiktor et al. 2000).

Internal: Relatively small genitalia; epiphallus joins on side apex of penis (Wiktor 2001); short epiphallus and vas deferens; short, thin oviduct; wide penial retractor; spermatheca with thick, cylindrical duct (Wiktor et al. 2000).

Unique characters of A. yunnanensis among Anadenus are very wide, triangular-in-cross-section wrinkles and short vas deferens (Wiktor 2001).
